Giovanna, hi, it is Greg. Are you busy right now?
A little. I am measuring the tunnel wall at the moment. But go ahead.
I need one number for my report. What are you doing tomorrow morning?
Tomorrow? On Tuesdays I usually work in the office, so I am free after nine.
Good. And your team, what are they doing today?
They are waiting for a delivery. The truck is late again.
Same here. We always wait for something. Can you take a look at the drawing tonight?
Sorry, could you say that again, please? A machine is passing behind me.
Of course. Can you take a look at the drawing tonight, before the meeting?

Hi Giovanna, it is Karen. I am sending you a short one, because I am walking to the office right now and my hands are cold. Listen to my site at this moment. The big machine you can hear is cutting the wall, and two engineers are measuring the floor near the ramp. I usually work in the office in the morning, but today is different: I am outside, and I am waiting for a delivery. The truck is late, as always. My boss is having a meeting with the client at the moment, so nobody is answering the phone. Talk to you later.

Good afternoon, everyone. Ray Collins, with a short update for the afternoon shift. Right now the north area is closed, because the crew is moving the big containers. They are working there until four. If you are waiting for a delivery, please hold on: the trucks are coming in through the south gate today, not the main gate. I am taking a look at the schedule for tomorrow, and one thing is already clear: the morning meeting is starting at seven, not at eight. Nobody is late tomorrow, please. Thank you, and stay safe.
